items.title: Inflation Is Hot, So Why Will the Fed Hold This Week?
items.summary: Inflation is running hot and the Fed raised rates just last month. Yet futures markets put the odds of another hike at this week's meeting at only about 10%. In this video, Eric Bleeker, CFA, Chief Investment Officer of 24/7 Wall St., explains why Wall Street expects the Federal Reserve to sit still now, and why December looks very different, with hike odds above 80%. With consumer prices up 3.7% and the 10-year Treasury yield near 5%, the biggest questions are how Fed Chair Kevin Warsh explains a pause, and what his move away from forward guidance means for markets. We'll also cover the political pressure on the Fed from the White House, and what Morgan Stanley (NYSE: MS) strategists say a few more hikes would mean for the bull market. Finally, we'll lay out what to watch: Wednesday's Fed statement, Warsh's press conference, and the inflation and jobs reports that could lock in a December hike.
